conversation:
Patient: I'm 52 years old, and I'm here because I've been having a lot of pain on the inside of my right elbow. It's been hurting for about four days now, and it's really bad—it's a seven out of ten. It even wakes me up at night, and it's making it hard for me to work on my pottery, which I've been really into lately.
Doctor: Could you please confirm your age, gender, and describe the nature of the pain in your right elbow, including any activities that aggravate or relieve it?
Patient: Sure, I'm 52 years old, and I'm a woman. The pain is on the inside of my right elbow, and it hurts when I try to do things like bend my wrist or use my arm for pottery. It doesn't really get better with anything I've tried, like ice or ibuprofen, and it's been getting me up at night.
Doctor: Have you experienced any recent trauma or injury to your right elbow, or do you have a history of repetitive use or occupational strain on that arm?
Patient: No, I don't think I've hit my elbow on anything, and I don't have a history of injury there. But I have been doing a lot of pottery lately, which involves using my arm a lot, and I think that's probably what's causing the pain.
Doctor: Have you experienced any swelling, redness, or stiffness in the affected elbow? Have you noticed any numbness or tingling in your hand or fingers?
Patient: No, I haven't noticed any swelling, redness, or stiffness in my elbow, and I don't have any numbness or tingling in my hand or fingers. It's just the pain on the inside of my elbow that's been really bothering me.
Doctor: Have you experienced any recent trauma or repetitive strain to the right elbow, and have you noticed any radiation of pain to your forearm or hand?
Patient: No, I don't think I've had any recent trauma to my elbow, but I have been doing a lot of pottery, which involves repetitive motions. The pain does radiate down my arm, along the inside of it, but I haven't felt anything in my hand or fingers.
Doctor: Have you experienced any clicking, locking, or popping sensations in your right elbow during the pain episodes?
Patient: No, I haven't felt any clicking, locking, or popping in my elbow during the pain episodes. It's just the constant ache on the inside that's been really bothering me, especially at night.
Doctor: Have you experienced any weakness in your grip or difficulty lifting objects with your right hand?
Patient: No, I haven't noticed any weakness in my grip or difficulty lifting objects with my right hand. I can still manage everyday tasks, but it's really hard to work on my pottery because of the pain. It's been so bad that it's keeping me up at night.
Doctor: Have you experienced any previous episodes of elbow pain or been diagnosed with any musculoskeletal or autoimmune conditions in the past?
Patient: No, I don't think I've had any previous episodes of elbow pain, and I don't have any musculoskeletal or autoimmune conditions that I'm aware of. This is the first time I've experienced pain like this in my elbow.
Doctor: Have you undergone any imaging studies such as X-rays or MRI of the right elbow in the past, and if so, what were the findings?
Patient: No, I don't think I've had any imaging studies of my elbow in the past. The doctor did order an X-ray today, and I was told it looked great—no fractures or bony abnormalities. I don't know the exact details, but it seems like it's not a structural issue.
Doctor: Have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your hand or fingers, especially on the side of your little finger and ring finger, which could suggest ulnar nerve involvement?
Patient: No, I haven't experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in my hand or fingers, especially on the side of my little finger and ring finger. I just have this constant ache on the inside of my elbow that radiates down my arm, but my hand and fingers feel normal.
Doctor: Could you describe any specific movements or activities related to your pottery work that seem to make the pain worse?
Patient: Well, I've been using my right arm a lot on the pottery wheel, especially when I'm shaping the clay and trying to get the bowl just right. It's the repetitive motion of turning the wheel and pressing into the clay that seems to make it worse. I think that's been putting a lot of strain on my elbow.
Doctor: Have you noticed any swelling, redness, or warmth around your right elbow, or any stiffness in the joint that makes it difficult to move your arm?
Patient: No, I haven't noticed any swelling, redness, or warmth around my right elbow, and my joint doesn't feel stiff. It's just this deep ache that's been getting me pretty frustrated, especially since I can't work on my pottery like I want to. It's really affecting my ability to do something I love.
Doctor: Have you experienced any recent changes in the strength of your right hand or fingers, or any difficulty performing fine motor tasks with your right hand?
Patient: No, I haven't noticed any changes in the strength of my right hand or fingers, and I don't have any difficulty performing fine motor tasks with my right hand. My hand feels normal, and I can still grip things and move my fingers without any trouble. It's just the elbow that's been giving me a lot of pain.
Doctor: Have you noticed any swelling, redness, or warmth around your right elbow that might suggest inflammation or infection?
Patient: No, I haven't noticed any swelling, redness, or warmth around my right elbow. It doesn't look inflamed or infected—it just feels tender and aches a lot, especially when I try to use my arm for pottery. The doctor said the X-ray looked good, so I guess it's not a structural issue.
Doctor: Have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your forearm or hand that could suggest nerve involvement, such as ulnar nerve entrapment?
Patient: No, I haven't experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in my forearm or hand. My hand feels normal, and I can still grip things and move my fingers without any trouble. It's just the elbow that's been giving me a lot of pain.
